criteria.quote: Grimer Is Starving Because Water Got Cleaner
criteria.revision: Change the title to “Grimer Is Starving Because Factory Wastewater Got Cleaner” to make the contradiction more specific and match the research.

criteria.quote: Grimer’s main food is slimy industrial waste from factories.
criteria.revision: Keep the factory-waste detail, but replace “water” elsewhere with “factory wastewater” so the story does not broaden the research into a claim about clean water generally.

criteria.quote: How can cleaner wastewater push a Pokémon toward extinction?
criteria.revision: Delay the explanation in the opening narration: change it to “Factory wastewater is clean these days. Why would that leave Grimer with nothing to eat?” Then reveal the answer in the next scene.

criteria.quote: Then clean factory wastewater leaves Grimer with nothing to eat.
criteria.revision: Cut the redundant “THE FOOD SOURCE VANISHED” scene and let the sequence escalate from factory waste, to sewer-pipe feeding, to the stronger biological consequence: “In a sterile environment, Grimer’s germs can’t multiply, and it dies.”

criteria.quote: Sterile environments stop its germs from multiplying, and Grimer dies.
criteria.revision: Frame this as the reveal after establishing its diet: “But food isn’t the only problem: in a sterile environment, Grimer’s germs can’t multiply, and it dies.”

criteria.quote: Cleaner factory water may push Grimer toward extinction.
criteria.revision: Remove or substantially reframe the later “THE FOOD SOURCE VANISHED” scene, since it repeats the opening threat. Use the later beat only for the distinct fact that sterile environments prevent Grimer’s germs from multiplying and cause it to die.

criteria.quote: Grimer turns a polluted world into food, yet sterile environments can make it die.
criteria.revision: Strengthen the payoff with the two separate dependencies: “Factory wastewater is Grimer’s main food, but in a sterile environment its germs can’t multiply—and Grimer dies.”

criteria.quote: Which matters more: clean wastewater or Grimer’s food supply?
